subject: Private deployment — econ bands, support tier, and environment sizing follow-up
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Reed <sam.reed@acme-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: private deployment economics and next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the demo and the candid run-through of Acme's usage patterns earlier today. As promised, a concise recap and a couple of qualification questions so we can size an accurate private/VPC proposal: 

1) Baseline token profile: you said ~150M generated tokens / month today with spikes up to ~350M during peak campaigns — confirm if those are generated-only or include input tokens.
2) Budget band target: you mentioned a mid-range annual spend target for inference of $120k–$400k. Can you confirm whether that is OPEX-only (hosted/inference) or if you have a combined OPEX + CapEx target for on-prem tooling/maintenance?
3) Environments: you indicated 3 logical environments (dev/stage/prod) with prod having dedicated capacity. Is that still accurate and do you expect additional regional prod environments?
4) Support & SLA: which support tier do you expect to need — business hours with 24hr response, or 24x7 critical response + monthly review?

Attached: a short econ summary (redwood-econ-summary.pdf) and an editable workbook for the token bands (Acme_MA_Pricing_Workbook.xlsx).

If you can answer 1–4, we’ll run two price options: (A) annual reserved license + 8x environment slab (predictable throughput), (B) quarterly committed capacity with burst credits and a lower base license (better for variable spikes). We'll also surface a target $/1M tokens metric for each option so you can compare to your internal $/1M benchmark.

Proposed next step: quick 30m call Tuesday to confirm token accounting and pick a preferred licensing path.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0119

Attachment: Acme_MA_Pricing_Workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: redwood-econ-summary.pdf (one-pager)

From: Sam Reed <sam.reed@acme-health.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: engops@acme-health.com
Date: 2026-10-05T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: private deployment economics and next steps

Tessa —

Thanks for the recap and the attachments. Quick answers inline: 

1) Token profile: the numbers I gave earlier are total tokens (inputs + outputs). Typical prompt/input is small (~30 tokens) but outputs average 120 tokens.
2) Budget band: that $120k–$400k was a FY27 OPEX planning number for inference only. There will be a separate capital bucket for on-prem appliance purchases if we go that route.
3) Environments: dev/stage/prod only, no extra regions for now — prod single region with HA pair.
4) Support: we need at least business hours + 24hr critical. We may upgrade to 24x7 after pilot if latency/regulatory demands increase.

One more data point: our legal team is pushing for an annual licensing structure (simpler procurement) but engops prefers the commit + burst model to control cost during marketing spikes. We want both options quantified.

Also — timeline: procurement prefers vendor shortlist by end of Oct; aiming for pilot contract signed by mid-Nov.

—Sam
Sam Reed
Director, Engineering Ops
Acme Health
sam.reed@acme-health.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: private deployment economics and next steps (internal)

Internal notes for proposal build — tagging here so we have a single source of truth: 

- Use two canonical econ templates:
  A) Annual license + dedicated envs: assume 3 envs (dev/stage/prod) with prod HA pair. Price components: base platform license, per-GPU reserved slab, optional paid support tier (enterprise). Target unit metric: $/1M tokens = derived from (license + reserved GPU amortized + support) / expected tokens.
  B) Commit + burst model: lower base license, committed monthly token throughput (3 bands: 100M, 250M, 500M) with overage priced per 1M tokens and burst credits for 24hr spikes. Include annual true-up.

- For Acme numbers: use the OPEX band $120k–$400k to reverse-engineer target $/1M tokens. If they sit at 150M–350M tokens/month (1.8B–4.2B tokens/year) then $120k/yr implies ~$28–$67 per 1M tokens; $400k/yr implies ~$94–$222 per 1M tokens. We should show three anchor points (low/expected/high).

- Support tiers: list Business (Mon–Fri 8–6, 24hr critical), Enterprise (24x7 critical, monthly review, dedicated TAM) with associated percent uplift on license (e.g., +12% / +22%).

- Ask legal for preferred contract term: 12 vs 36 months. If legal prefers annual licensing, provide blended amortized on-prem purchase optionally modeled as CapEx conversion in appendix.

Next actions: Tessa to run the workbook and send two option sheets to Sam by EOD tomorrow. Vivek to sanity-check unit economics for the prod HA pair (GPU count) and confirm expected token throughput per GPU assumption.

-Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Reed <sam.reed@acme-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: private deployment economics and next steps

Sam —

Appreciate the fast clarifications. We’ll do exactly that: two clear options (annual license + reserved envs vs commit + burst) with per-1M-token targets shown at three usage anchors. Expect the workbook back to you by tomorrow EOD with a short commentary page that maps each option to procurement preferences (simplicity vs cost-flexibility).

Quick clarifying question for procurement: when you say "vendor shortlist by end of Oct" — does procurement need a PO-ready SOW (price + SLAs) for shortlist inclusion, or is a term-sheet/ballpark pricing OK? If they want PO-ready, we’ll fast-track legal for a minimal SOW.

Proposed next step: 30m sync Wednesday 10/7 at 10:00am PT to review the workbook. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite now.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Acme into pilot.

Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
